correctness.rationale: For any nonempty family of models, either there is one component or two components supply distinct U-witnesses with no cross E-edge, proving closure. On exactly specified two- and three-element structures, only the smaller satisfies Psi. Every relation-closed induced embedding preserves all allowed matrices forward by induction on atomic/negated atomic, Boolean, existential and guarded-universal constructors. Two embeddings of the smaller structure cover the larger one, so the conjectured universal formula cannot distinguish them. The proof covers arbitrary models and all formula ranks; 6561 finite pairs and witness maps are independently tested.

value.rationale: The identity-free case is explicitly named an open problem by a current 2026 primary source. A direct two-relation counterexample answers it negatively even for finite structures, identifies a sharp semantic obstruction to the proposed normal form via relation-closed embedding covers, and distinguishes one-way union preservation from invariance. It is a motivated structural resolution, not a mere table computation or arbitrary finite slice.
